destination.name: Úbeda
destination.description:
Important and populous city located on the hills of its name, in the geographic center of the province, in a landscape filled with olive trees and cereal fields.

Úbeda is an artistic and monumental city, no matter where you look, and one of the most noble and glorious towns in Andalusia. Renaissance from every angle, it contains such a quantity of monuments, churches, palaces, and manor houses that the best thing to do is to stroll through it and virtually transport oneself to the time of its historical splendor: The Sacred Chapel of the Savior, located in the incomparable Vázquez de Molina square, the Church of San Pablo, the Minor Basilica of Santa María de los Reales Alcázares, the Church of the Trinity, the Oratory of San Juan de la Cruz, Royal Monastery of Santa Clara, Monastery of the Conception, Vela de los Cobos Palace, Palace of the Chains, House of the Towers, Hospital of Santiago, Hospital of the Honored Old Men of the Savior, Clock Tower, Walls of the Cava, Pottery Museum, and the Dean Ortega Palace, currently a National Parador of Tourism, are some of the wonders contained in this surprising city.

In addition to these attractions, a visit to the walls and the splendid view that can be obtained from there is suggested; and to its potters, especially the house-museum of Paco Tito.

trips.name: Pottery District and Santo Tomás Route
trips.description:
In 2012, Úbeda was declared an "Area of Artisanal Interest in Andalusia." The declaration recognizes the relevance and uniqueness of the city''s crafts, as well as the diversity of existing trades and the artistic quality of the pieces, which combine tradition with new designs.

The surviving artisanal trades reflect a long historical experience: pottery, artistic forging, cabinetmaking, artistic stained glass, vegetable fibers, and Mudejar coffered ceilings are some of the sectors in which the artisans excel, exporting their production to various parts of the national and international geography. Each of their products enjoys the exclusivity and authenticity characteristic of handmade items, resulting from the transformation of noble materials with traditional techniques. Additionally, they have significant recognitions within the artisanal world (Master Craftsmen, National Craftsmanship Award, National Design Award...).

Any object produced in the workshops of Úbeda, whether large or small, simple or complex, is today a museum piece, worthy of being preserved and admired.

trips.name: Southern Renaissance Route
trips.description: This route begins at Plaza Vázquez de Molina. This square constitutes the most important monumental complex of the city and corresponds to the so-called Exceptional Universal Value, EUV, for which UNESCO declared the city of Úbeda a World Heritage Site on July 3, 2003. Made up of a group of civil and religious buildings constructed in just fifty years, it forms the great Renaissance architectural ensemble of Spain and one of the most important in Europe.

trips.name: Religious Tourism
trips.description:
If Úbeda had to be defined by a single slogan, it would be "City for the Spirit", as every corner of the city invites elevation: few cities are so conducive to the expression of intimate religiosity and a sense of transcendence. In this regard, the influence of Saint John of the Cross is unavoidable, a city that built the first temple in the Catholic world in his honor and which today preserves an important cultural heritage linked to the saint and poet.

The religious heritage preserved in convents and churches is very rich, and will soon be significantly enriched with the return to the Chapel of El Salvador of the sculpture of San Juanito, recently restored in Florence and the only work by Michelangelo in Spain.

The popular expression of religiosity reaches its climax each year during HOLY WEEK, a grand event with its own unique character made up of Castilian and Andalusian elements. With almost twenty brotherhoods—several of them centuries-old—, Holy Week is configured as a total celebration: an impressive collection of the best post-war imagery, its own gastronomy, and a series of deep-rooted traditions among which the Magna General Procession on Good Friday stands out.

trips.name: Monuments
trips.description:
The monuments of Úbeda constitute one of the most important heritage sites in Andalusia and throughout Spain. The city stands out for its extraordinary Renaissance architecture, internationally recognized after being declared a World Heritage Site by UNESCO. Walking through Úbeda is to discover palaces, churches, and civil buildings that reflect the artistic and political splendor experienced during the 16th and 17th centuries.

Among the most emblematic monuments is the Plaza Vázquez de Molina, considered one of the most beautiful Renaissance squares in Europe. It is home to architectural gems such as the Sacra Capilla del Salvador, the Palacio de las Cadenas, and the Old Granary, which make this space the monumental heart of the city.

The Sacra Capilla del Salvador is one of the great symbols of Úbeda and a must-visit. Its monumental facade and richly decorated interior reflect the importance of the Spanish Renaissance and the power of its promoters.

Other notable monuments include the Minor Basilica of Santa María de los Reales Alcázares, the Hospital de Santiago—known as the "Andalusian Escorial"—and numerous noble palaces that dot the historic center.

Visiting the monuments of Úbeda is to immerse oneself in centuries of history, art, and culture, enjoying a unique monumental environment that makes the city an essential destination for heritage lovers.

trips.name: Museum and Interpretation Centers
trips.description:
The museums and interpretation centers in Úbeda complement its monumental offer and allow for a deeper understanding of the city''s history, art, and traditions. These spaces offer visitors a complete and enriching cultural experience.

The Renaissance Interpretation Center is key to understanding the importance of Úbeda during this historical period. Through audiovisual resources and educational exhibitions, visitors can contextualize the value of the monumental complex.

Other museums and exhibition spaces cover themes such as archaeology, sacred art, or the culture of olive oil, one of the major economic and cultural pillars of the region.

These centers are designed for all types of audiences, from families to specialized visitors, and allow for an accessible, enjoyable, and educational visit.

The museums of Úbeda turn the visit into a complete cultural experience, ideal for those who wish to know the city beyond its streets and monuments.

trips.name: Archaeological Sites
trips.description:
The archaeological sites of Úbeda and its surroundings:

The archaeological sites of the Eras del Alcázar and the Ruins of Santo Tomás are part of the heritage wealth of Úbeda and contribute to reinforcing its historical identity. These spaces allow us to understand how the city has been built over time, from its earliest settlements to the present day.

Moreover, these archaeological sites represent an opportunity to enjoy a different cultural experience, where history, archaeology, and tourism combine to offer visitors a more complete view of Úbeda. The conservation and enhancement of these sites reflect the city''s commitment to its heritage and the dissemination of its cultural legacy.

Visiting these spaces not only means discovering archaeological remains but also participating in the living history of Úbeda. Each visit contributes to the valorization of these places and to the knowledge of a heritage that belongs to everyone.

Úbeda is internationally recognized for its extraordinary historical and artistic heritage. Its Renaissance streets, monumental architecture, and rich cultural tradition make this enclave one of the most fascinating destinations in southern Spain. However, beyond its squares and emblematic buildings, Úbeda still holds treasures that allow traveling to older times and understanding the origin and evolution of the city. Among them, the archaeological sites of the Eras del Alcázar and the Ruins of Santo Tomás stand out, two spaces that offer a unique experience to discover history from its foundations.

trips.name: Other Places of Tourist Interest
trips.description:
In addition to its monumental complex, Úbeda has numerous tourist attractions that enrich the visit. Natural viewpoints, historic neighborhoods, charming squares, and cultural spaces complete the experience.

The natural environment surrounding the city offers unique landscapes dominated by a sea of olive trees. These places allow you to discover a quieter and more authentic Úbeda, away from the better-known routes.

Exploring other corners of Úbeda is to be surprised by a city full of nuances and charm.

Úbeda is committed to inclusive and accessible tourism, working to ensure that all people can enjoy its heritage and cultural offerings on equal terms. Tourism for all is a commitment to diversity and the continuous improvement of the tourist experience.

The city has accessible itineraries, adapted spaces, and informational resources that facilitate the visit for people with reduced mobility, functional diversity, or special needs. The goal is to eliminate barriers and promote a fairer and more respectful tourism.

Many of Úbeda''s main monuments and cultural spaces incorporate accessibility measures, allowing a greater number of people to learn about and enjoy its historical and artistic richness.

Additionally, tourist information is offered in various formats, facilitating understanding and access to content. This contributes to each visitor being able to organize their visit according to their needs and preferences.

Úbeda thus establishes itself as a destination committed to tourism for all, where accessibility and inclusion are part of its identity as an open and welcoming city.
